meta.title: Grandma's Recipe
meta.blurb: Every year, Grandma Zefa wins the cocada contest. This year, Joana must cook, but one ingredient in the old recipe is missing! You decide what she does.

p1.title: The Old Notebook
text: Every year, Vó Zefa made cocada for the cooking contest at the town festival, and every year she won. But this year, she was away. She was visiting her sister in another state.
“You can make the cocada this year,” she said to Joana on the phone. “My recipe is in the old blue notebook.”
On Friday, Joana found the notebook. But there was a coffee [[stain|mancha]] on the page, and she couldn't read one [[ingredient|ingrediente]]! The contest was on Sunday.

p2a.title: A Bad Call
text: Joana called Vó Zefa. The phone line was terrible. “The secret ingredient is... is...” said Grandma. Then the call ended.
Joana tried again three times, but Grandma's phone was off. Her little brother, Nino, laughed. “Maybe the secret is chocolate!”
“It isn't chocolate,” said Joana. Then she thought about lime. Lime was in many of Grandma's recipes.

question.q: Why couldn't Joana hear the secret ingredient?

p2b.title: The First Try
text: Joana made cocada with coconut, sugar and milk, but without the secret ingredient. First, she cooked everything for forty minutes. Then she waited for it to cool.
Her little brother, Nino, tasted it. “It's OK,” he said. “But Grandma's cocada is better.”
Joana looked at the notebook again. Maybe there were more pages. Or maybe Dona Lurdes, the neighbor, knew the secret. She was Grandma's old friend.

p3x.title: Lime
text: Joana put lime in the cocada. First, she used one lime. Then she used two. Nino tasted it and made a funny face. “It's [[sour|azedo]]!” he said.
Joana tried again with less lime. It was better, but it wasn't Grandma's cocada.
It was nine o'clock on Saturday night. The contest was the next day.

p3y.title: Dona Lurdes
text: Dona Lurdes opened the door with a big smile. She was in the cooking contest too! Joana showed her the notebook.
Dona Lurdes read the page for a long time. “Zefa and I were friends for fifty years,” she said. “I know this recipe. The secret is a little [[ginger|gengibre]].”
Joana was surprised. Was it true? Or did Dona Lurdes want to win the contest?

p3z.title: The Last Page
text: Joana looked at every page of the old notebook. Finally, on the last page, she found a small note in Grandma's [[handwriting|letra]]:
“My cocada secret: a [[pinch|pitada]] of salt and a lot of love. — Zefa”
“Salt?” said Nino. “In a sweet?” Joana laughed. It was strange, but it was Grandma's handwriting. Then Joana looked at the clock. It was late, and she was tired.

p4a.title: All Night
text: Joana cooked all night. First, she tried cocada with orange. Then she tried it with pineapple. At four in the morning, she made a cocada with passion fruit, and it was delicious!
But Joana was very tired. Her eyes were red, and her hands were full of sugar.
The contest started at ten.

p4b.title: Joana's Cocada
text: On Sunday, the town square was full of music and food. Joana put her cocada on the contest table, next to Dona Lurdes's cocada and ten others.
It wasn't Grandma's recipe. It was Joana's own recipe, and she was a little nervous.
Later, the three judges tasted it. “Hmm,” said one judge. “Is this the famous Zefa recipe?”

p4c.title: The Ginger
text: Joana put a little ginger in the cocada. Then she tasted it. It was exactly like Grandma's cocada! Dona Lurdes told the truth.
On Sunday morning, Dona Lurdes knocked on the door. “Joana, my oven broke,” she said sadly. “I can't make my cocada for the contest.”

p4d.title: A Pinch of Salt
text: Joana made the cocada again with a pinch of salt. It was perfect! She put it in the fridge and went to bed happy.
On Sunday morning, she opened the fridge. Half of the cocada wasn't there! Nino was on the sofa with a big smile and sugar on his face.
The contest started in one hour.

e1.title: Grandma's Pride
text: The judges tasted the cocada and closed their eyes. “This is the real Zefa cocada!” said one of them.
In the end, Joana won first prize. That night, she called Grandma on video. Vó Zefa cried with happiness. “Now the recipe is yours too,” she said.
e1.eventPt: a Joana ganhou o primeiro prêmio

e2.title: A New Recipe
text: “No,” said Joana. “This is my own recipe. I didn't know Grandma's secret.” The judges smiled. They liked her honesty, and they loved the cocada.
Joana won a special prize for the best new recipe. Later, Grandma called. “Next year, you can teach me your recipe!” she said.
e2.event: she won a prize for a new recipe
e2.eventPt: ela ganhou um prêmio por uma receita nova

question.q: Why did the judges like Joana?

e3.title: The Sleepy Cook
text: The passion fruit cocada was delicious, and many people wanted to buy it. But Joana was so tired that she fell asleep on a chair next to the table.
The judges wanted to talk to her, but she didn't wake up. In the end, she got third place, and Nino sold all the cocada.

e4.title: Second Place
text: Joana's cocada was great, and she won second place. But Dona Lurdes didn't enter the contest this year, and she watched it alone and sad.
Later, Joana thought about her. “Next year, we cook together,” she said. Dona Lurdes smiled for the first time that day.

options: When Joana talked about next year

e5.title: Too Late
text: Joana ran to the town square with her cocada. But when she arrived, the judges were leaving. The contest ended at eleven.
Joana sat on a bench, sad. Then an old man tasted her cocada. “Delicious!” he said. It wasn't a prize, but it helped a little.
e5.event: she arrived late at the contest

e6.title: Not Grandma's
text: “Yes, it's Grandma's recipe,” said Joana. But one of the judges was Grandma's old friend. She tasted the cocada and shook her head.
“This isn't Zefa's cocada,” she said. The judges didn't give Joana a prize. Later, Joana understood: her own cocada was good, but the lie wasn't.
